sanskrit_verse:
करिष्यति वृषोत्सर्गम् इष्टापूर्तं तथैव च /
पालयिष्यति वार्धक्ये श्राद्धं दास्यति चान्वहम् // BrhS_1,26.91
transliteration: kariṣyati vṛṣotsargam iṣṭāpūrtaṃ tathaiva ca / pālayiṣyati vārdhakye śrāddhaṃ dāsyati cānvaham
sph_interpretive_translation: One who performs the ritual release of a bull, conducts prescribed sacrifices and offerings, protects during old age, offers timely oblations to ancestors, and gives regularly—such a person upholds Dharma through action and sustains cosmic order.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from alignment with Dharma-sustaining actions
Causation arises from intentional acts that uphold ancestral and societal continuity
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's ability to perform sustaining rituals and give appropriately
Restoration logic operates through completion of prescribed duties and offerings
Consciousness alignment manifests when personal conduct mirrors universal sacrificial order
executable_legal_axioms: IF agent performs vṛṣotsarga AND iṣṭāpūrta THEN agent contributes positively to dharmic balance
IF agent reaches vārdhakya AND fails to perform śrāddha THEN initiate capacity-restoring protocol via family or community
IF agent demonstrates consistent anvaha dāna THEN assign higher ritual participation rights within jurisdiction
IF agent omits all three duties for >1 year THEN invoke consciousness-reintegration process before civil privileges are restored
supreme_court_application: At the Supreme Court level, this verse establishes thresholds for determining whether an individual has fulfilled their foundational obligations to society and cosmos. The court must assess not intent but actual performance of vṛṣotsarga, iṣṭāpūrta, and śrāddha as markers of lawful integration in the dharmic social fabric. Failure in these indicates a need for restorative protocols rather than punitive exclusion.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa shows clear causal sequence: ritual action → ancestral satisfaction → societal harmony. Anupūrvaśaḥ confirms sequential unfolding of consequence based on omission or commission. Proportional responsibility lies in re-engagement with the specific omitted duty. Non-punitive reality rule affirms that correction occurs through completion, not suffering.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Assign supervised performance of missed vṛṣotsarga and śrāddha under qualified priestly oversight
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Require public declaration of renewed commitment to iṣṭāpūrta and anvaha dāna
Capacity Restoration Mechanism: Provide financial and logistical support to enable full resumption of elder-care and offering practices
Integrity Reintegration Sequence: Conduct ceremonial purification followed by community acknowledgment of renewed dharmic standing
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established. Dharma is restored through right action. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness alone is the ultimate adjudicator.
